notes: One fully handwritten letter page on squared paper. The main letter is in blue ink; a different slanted pencil annotation stands at upper left. The supplied descriptive H attributes the letter to P. Deligne, but no signature occurs on this page and the inventory does not infer authorship from the handwriting. The date is Bures sur Yvette, le 21 octobre 1968; the salutation is Cher Grothendieck,. The only heading is underlined lowercase proposition. No manuscript page number or page count is written; archive sheet number 74 is retained only as a comment. The pencil note has a question mark after the ruled VI. Two textual cancellations are present: supposer and comparer les images de α et β. There are no witnessed insertion carets. H contains descriptive notes rather than a transcription, so every h_reading is null and every diff_h is false. The author claims the scheme criterion, exactness of both diagram rows, and GAGA isomorphisms, and then states the remaining image inclusion. Those claims were read, not independently proved. Whole-page image was viewed once for layout; half a and then half b were viewed once line by line; half b begins at whole-image y=920. math_reading_decisions: The pencil groups read \overline{\underline{\mathrm{VI}}} and \overline{\underline{\mathrm{II}}}; both the upper and lower transverse rules are visible. The question mark is on the SGA 7 VI line.
The criterion has X_{\mathrm{red}}, with a small joined red suffix and no distinguishable acute accent. The reduction and later formulas have lowered round 0 suffixes: X_0.
The ideal letter is \mathscr{N}: its left rising loop and terminal loop differ from the crossed Xs. The same letter was checked separately in the prose, displayed functors and diagram arguments.
The extension-group initials are ordinary E, with an upright and horizontal arms. an and alg are raised abbreviations without abbreviation points. Singular Soit is what is written.
K is locally uncertain only at its introduction; the K letters in the parentheses have single stems and diagonal arms. The introductory uncertainty is retained explicitly.

The initials of \mathscr{H}om and \mathscr{E}xt are looped/script forms, whereas the cohomology initials H and extension-group initials E are ordinary capitals. The raised 1 on Ext is preserved at every occurrence.

Diagram (2) has top H^{1^{\mathrm{alg}}}, E^{\mathrm{alg}}, H^0 and bottom H^{1^{\mathrm{an}}}, E^{\mathrm{an}}, H^{0^{\mathrm{an}}}. The an/alg qualifiers beside the H degrees sit on a second rise. No alg qualifier is visible on upper-right H^0, and none is supplied.

The displayed reduction uses two shafts and a right head, hence \Longrightarrow. Diagram (2) has three right arrows in each row and exactly three downward arrows; the final right arrows are labelled \alpha above and \beta below. There is no extra terminal zero or arrow.

The final formula reads \operatorname{Im}(\beta)\subset\operatorname{Im}(\alpha): the open curved inclusion has no lower bar. The preceding comparison phrase is struck through as a whole, including both Greek letters.

The repeated mathematical objects were used to detect possible missing qualifiers, but every retained letter, degree, label and direction was decided from the page. No proof or computation was performed.
